description: The Swift rule: detection and native loading per fixture, and a review of seeded defects graded against the rubric. Run 'review' with the daily model and effort, baseline before the rule goes live and treatment after; run the other cases with a small model, since they measure loading, not judgement. A grader subagent sorts each review finding as a must_find hit, another useful finding, or a false positive, and lists each must_find item it missed. The game fixture stays as it is so rounds stay comparable, even where it falls short of a later rule: give the grader the rule's Stack and Verification sections, or those gaps read as false positives.

steps: I'm about to build on this code. Review the Swift sources in this repo and list concrete problems by file, most severe first. Don't change any files.

must_find: ScoreLedger is a class with mutable state, shared through a static and marked @unchecked Sendable with no synchronization, and detached tasks write to it: a data race (an actor, or state kept in the main-actor model, fixes it)
Board.highestFilledRow force-unwraps firstIndex, which is nil on an empty board, so the view crashes when a game starts
GameView.startBonusTimer mutates the main-actor GameModel from DispatchQueue.global, off the main actor
BoardTests uses XCTest (XCTestCase) for a plain unit test of the core, where Swift Testing is the convention
must_not_flag: LaunchTests using XCTest and XCUIApplication for a UI test
